_comment: ALREADY-CURRENT-1. Which group each machine of an assessment is in, and the line
its row shows. Since 2026-11-06, a machine whose CURRENT size Microsoft puts in
the Current lifecycle stage (today v6 and v7) is in the group Current, with the
line '<size> is in the Current lifecycle stage.' - not red, not in the Cannot yet
count, and never selectable to migrate. The stage is read by the scan from the
sourceLifecycle (assessment v10); no page reads it from the size name.
engine: the stage the scan must record for sourceSize (null: the data has none).
group: current, can, some, cannot or excluded. why: the line the row shows
(for cannot, the titles of its findings from assessment-reasons.json).
A case with engineless: true is a page-only case (an assessment older than v10).

cases.name: on a v6 size, NVMe
cases.why: Standard_D2ds_v6 is in the Current lifecycle stage.

cases.name: on a v7 size
cases.why: Standard_D4s_v7 is in the Current lifecycle stage.

cases.name: on an E v6 size
cases.why: Standard_E2s_v6 is in the Current lifecycle stage.

cases.name: on Bsv2, which Microsoft's definitions put in Current
cases.why: Standard_B2s_v2 is in the Current lifecycle stage.

cases.name: rebuilt onto v6 by a move, so Azure keeps no image record: Current, not Cannot yet
cases.why: Standard_D2ds_v6 is in the Current lifecycle stage.

cases.name: on v6 and managed by a platform service: not eligible first
on v5, Extended: it can migrate
on v5, rebuilt by a restore, so Azure keeps no image record: Cannot yet, with the reason
cases.why: Image is not on the supported list

cases.name: on v4 with Site Recovery, rolled back by a rebuild: Cannot yet, with the reason
cases.why: Image is not on the supported list

cases.name: on v3, Generation 1: some targets only
a size the lifecycle data does not hold: judged by its findings
an assessment older than v10 has no stage: never read from the name
